```{r}
#Installing and importing libraries

#import libraries
#install.packages("fixest")
#install.packages("gt")
#install.packages("broom")
#install.packages("purrr")
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)
library(broom)
library(purrr)
```

### Ploting the comparison trend

```{r}
df1 <- read_excel("Alcohol Consumption Data.xlsx", sheet = "Graph 1")
ggplot(df1, aes(x = Year)) +
  #Plot California trend line with dots
  geom_line(aes(y = CA, color = "CA"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = CA, color = "CA"), size = 2) +
  #Plot control trend line with dots
  geom_line(aes(y = ControlledStateAverage, color = "Controlled State Average"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ControlledStateAverage, color = "Controlled State Average"), size = 2) +
  #Indicate when treatment is applied
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2018, linetype = "dashed") +
  #Labeling
  labs(
    title = "Legal Recreational Marijuana's Effects on Alcohol Consumption",
    subtitle = "Marijuana Introduction in CA = 2018",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Alcohol Consumption (Gallons of Ethanol Per Capita)",
    color = "State"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()
```



### Plotting Counterfactual Trend


```{r}
#Import data again
df2 <- read_excel("Alcohol Consumption Data.xlsx", sheet = "Graph 1")

# Compute pre-treatment gap (CA - control)
pre_gap <- df2 |>
  filter(Year < 2018) |>
  summarise(gap = mean(CA - ControlledStateAverage)) |>
  pull(gap)

# Creating counterfactual: CA if no legalization of recerational marijuana
# This tests for parallel trend assumption
df2 <- df2 |>
  mutate(CA_counterfactual = ControlledStateAverage + pre_gap)

# Plot
ggplot(df2, aes(x = Year)) +
  #Graping three lines: actual treated, counterfactural, and control
  geom_line(aes(y = CA, color = "CA (Actual)"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ControlledStateAverage, color = "Control Avg"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = CA_counterfactual, color = "CA Counterfactual"), 
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  #Indicate the inception of treatment
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2018, linetype = "dashed") +
  #labeling
  labs(
    title = "Counterfactual Parallel Trend for CA",
    subtitle = "Dashed line shows expected CA alcohol consumption without legalization",
    y = "Alcohol Consumption (Gallons of Ethanol Per Capita)",
    x = "Year",
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Plotting Event Study Graph

```{r}
#Mutating CA for panel format
ca <- read_excel("Alcohol Consumption Data.xlsx", sheet = "Graph 1") |>
  select(Year, CA) |>
  rename(year = Year, y = CA) |>
  mutate(state = "CA")

#Mutating controls for panel format
control <- read_excel("Alcohol Consumption Data.xlsx", sheet = "Graph 2") |>
  select(-Average) |> #subtract "average" column
  rename(year = Year)|>
  pivot_longer(cols = -year, names_to = "state", values_to = "y")

#Combine CA with Controls
df3 <- bind_rows(ca, control) |>
  mutate(treated = (state == "CA"), #if treated
         post = (year >= 2018), #if it's post treatment
         did = treated * post, #if it's CA in post treatment
         treat_year = ifelse(state == "CA", 2018, 0)  # 0 = never-treated controls
  )

#Event Study Plot
es <- feols(y ~ sunab(treat_year, year) | state + year, data = df3, cluster = "state")
iplot(es,
      main = "Dynamic Impact of CA Recreational Marijuana Legalization",
      xlab = "Years Relative to Legalization",
      ylab = "Estimated Effect on Alcohol Consumption")
```

### Creating the Summary Statistics

```{r}
# Creating summary statistics
df_sum <- df3 |>
  mutate(
    #create grouping variables
    group = ifelse(state == "CA", "California", "Control States"),
    period = ifelse(year < 2018, "Pre-2018", "Post-2018")
  )

# Creating the summary table
datasummary(
  y ~ group * (Mean + SD + N),
  data = df_sum,
  title = "Summary Statistics: Alcohol Consumption by Group",
  output = "gt"
)
```

```{r}
#Creating model summary
m_did <- feols(y ~ did | state + year, data = df3, cluster = "state")
modelsummary(m_did,
             coef_map = c("did" = "California × Post (DiD Effect)"),
             statistic = "({std.error})",
             gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared"), #omits related outputs such as AIC, BIC, etc.
             title = "Difference-in-Differences Estimates of the Effect of Recreational Marijuana Legalization on Alcohol Consumption in CA"
)
```

### Conduct robustness check

```{r}

# Read your wide data
df3 <- read_excel("Alcohol Consumption Data.xlsx", sheet = "Graph 2")

# Keep actual state columns
control_states <- c("AL","AR","GA","FL","ID","IN","IA","KS","KY","LA",
                    "MS","NE","NC","SC","TN","TX","WI","WY")
all_states <- c("CA", control_states)

# Convert to long panel
df3 <- df3 |>
  select(Year, all_of(all_states)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -Year, names_to = "state", values_to = "alcohol") |>
  mutate(
    Post = if_else(Year >= 2018, 1, 0),
    CA = if_else(state == "CA", 1, 0)
  )

# Function to run DiD and return coefficient and CI
did <- function(data, label) {
  m <- lm(alcohol ~ CA*Post + factor(state) + factor(Year), data = data)
  out <- tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    filter(term == "CA:Post") |>
    transmute(
      spec = label,
      beta = estimate,
      se = std.error,
      p_value = p.value,
      ci_low = conf.low,
      ci_high = conf.high
    )
  out
}

#establishing baseline
baseline_results <- did(
  df3 |>
    filter(state %in% c("CA", control_states)),
  "Baseline"
)

#Excluding COVID years
covid_results <- did(
  df3 |> 
    filter(state %in% c("CA", control_states), Year <= 2019),
  "Exclude 2020–2022"
)

#Excluding one control robustness
control_results <- map_dfr(control_states, function(st) {
  did(
    df3 |> 
      filter(state %in% c("CA", setdiff(control_states, st))),
    paste("Drop", st)
  )
})

results_df <- bind_rows(baseline_results, covid_results, control_results)

# Order specs nicely
results_df <- results_df %>%
  mutate(spec = factor(spec, levels = rev(spec)))

# Plot robustness graph
ggplot(results_df, aes(x = beta, y = spec)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Robustness of DiD Estimate",
    subtitle = "Marijuana legalization and alcohol consumption in CA",
    x = "Estimated CA × Post Effect",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
